findings.what: Point 5: the `changes` line '+ hypothesis (1): M Hausdorff, tarentin and causal (DEC-22); without them the implication fails (Causal.not_causallyCompact_imp_causallyComplete, the bowtie, non-local)' is false. The bowtie is discrete, finite, Hausdorff, causal and tarentin (with p = q = x, J(x,x) = {x} is open), so it satisfies every hypothesis of (1). It refutes the old 'local causal chain' reading (CausallyComplete via IsMaximalChain/IsCausalChain), under which univ is a maximal chain. Under the DEC-21 reading the rewrite states, its maximal chains are the two-element sets {aᵢ, bⱼ}, which are Dedekind-complete. So the refutation is answered by the DEC-21 reading (stated explicitly in the rewrite), not by the added hypotheses.
findings.fix: Reword the line: the bowtie is answered by the DEC-21 reading of 'maximal chain' (it is causally complete in that reading); the hypotheses T2, tarentin, causal are those the proof of (1) uses (DEC-22), not ones the bowtie violates.
